A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LICO research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular optimization experiments, surrogate prediction comparisons, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds optimization results, backbone comparisons, GPT-4o prediction experiments, and evaluations of regressors using LLM embeddings.

M1.justification: The embedding and prediction layers, language instructions, semi-synthetic training objective, and optimization algorithm remain unchanged. Crossover and mutation, newly mentioned in the main method description, were already specified in v1 Appendix A.3. Additional backbone choices are experimental configurations.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from 21 to 23 molecular objectives by adding GSK3β and JNK3. ZINC 250K, the 47 intrinsic training properties, and the existing molecular tasks remain. The additional optimization budget changes the protocol rather than introducing a new domain.

E2.justification: The main comparison adds Genetic GFN, Augmented Memory, and MOLLEO, while removing TNP from the Top-10 comparison; TNP remains in the appendix Top-1/Top-100 tables. Appendices C.3–C.4 additionally evaluate GPT-4o and MLP/GP regressors using LLM embeddings.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 10,000-call evaluation using Llama-2-7B-32K-Instruct alongside the retained 1,000-call setting. Appendix B.1 reports tuning on five tasks and revises explicit baseline settings, including GP BO population size from 34 to 50 and Graph GA offspring count from 15 to 100. These reported changes do not establish that unchanged legacy scores were rerun.

E4.justification: The original language, synthetic-ratio, pretraining, and model-size ablations remain. New Appendices C.2–C.4 examine molecular pretraining through T5/Nach0 backbones, direct GPT-4o prompting, and LLM embeddings with conventional regressors. These substantially extend the analysis of which uses of LLMs support the method; the T5/Nach0 study evaluates prediction only.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed means and standard deviations for the main optimization comparisons. Additional results follow the existing reporting practice; no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Shared per-task scores in Table 1, original ablation values, and appendix Top-1/Top-100 results are retained. v2 adds results for new objectives and comparators, plus the full 10,000-call comparison: LICO totals 14.708, below Genetic GFN's 15.678 and Augmented Memory's 15.002. Figures 4–5 and Table 10 add prediction and embedding-comparison findings.

T1.justification: The optimization formulation, predictive distribution, training objective, GP/Tanimoto definition, and UCB formula are unchanged. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract changes from claiming state-of-the-art PMO performance to competitive performance on standard PMO and state of the art specifically on PMO-1K. This materially qualifies the central performance claim while retaining the methodological contribution. Section 6 nevertheless repeats the older, broader PMO claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations concerning molecular pretraining versus general pattern-matching capability, advantages of baselines that update during optimization, and speculative MOLLEO training contamination. It removes v1's explanation of GP BO improvements through candidate selection. The intrinsic-function availability limitation remains, while Appendix C.2 explicitly limits its backbone evidence to prediction rather than optimization.

D1.justification: v2 specifies exact Llama checkpoints and Liger Kernel use, baseline search grids and selected hyperparameters, the GPT-4o prompt, and embedding-MLP training details. Core LICO hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain. Removing the checklist also removes v1's promise to release code, data, and checkpoints; actual availability is not established by either PDF.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds substantial positioning against molecular LLM research, including MOLLEO, ChatDrug, BoChemian, Chemlactica/Chemma, MOLGEN, and DrugAssist, plus Optformer elsewhere in the discussion. It expands distinctions involving prompting, embeddings, and molecular finetuning. Updating the anonymous Bayesian-optimization citation to Liu et al. identifies an existing reference rather than adding a new work.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the introduction, method, and ablation prose remain intact. Changes include localized related-work and experiment rewrites, PMO-1K terminology, added appendix subsections, author-year citations, and removal of acknowledgements and the NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: Table 1 is restructured with more objectives and comparator columns and loses its mean-rank row. v2 adds the standard-budget results table, hyperparameter-search table, embedding-comparison table, and Figures 4–5. Existing figures and tables are retained or relocated and renumbered, while the document adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v1's broad performance claim rested on a restricted-budget evaluation with limited comparators. v2 substantially strengthens validation through standard-budget experiments, stronger molecular optimization baselines, and direct comparisons with alternative uses of LLMs. These reveal meaningful performance boundaries and support a more accurate abstract. The conclusion remains overbroad and some protocol reporting needs reconciliation, but the expanded, more relevant evidence substantially improves the paper's overall quality.
